title: CRM Implementation Services, Process and Cost | Stacktik
metaDescription: CRM implementation by Stacktik: the CRM chosen, set up and connected to calling and outreach, your data migrated, your team trained. Fixed fee in writing.
h1: CRM implementation for sales teams, from first call to handover.
lede: CRM implementation is the work of putting a CRM into daily use: choosing the system, setting it up around how your team sells, moving your data in, connecting calling, outreach and reporting, and training the people who use it.

summary.label: What it is
summary.text: Choosing a CRM, setting it up, migrating your data, connecting calling, outreach and reporting to it, and training your team to use it.

summary.label: Who it is for
summary.text: Sales and customer-facing teams choosing a first sales CRM, replacing one, or fixing a CRM that was bought but never set up properly.

summary.label: What you get
summary.text: A CRM configured in your own account, your data moved in, your other tools connected, recorded training sessions and written handover notes.

summary.label: How it is priced
summary.text: A fixed fee for the implementation, quoted in writing before work starts. Software stays on the vendor's own plan and pricing.

blocks.h2: What CRM implementation covers, from setup to CRM integration.
blocks.intro: A sales CRM is the system where every customer, opportunity and conversation lives. This list is what we draw from, not a fixed package.

items.title: CRM setup
items.body: Pipeline stages, with written rules for when an opportunity moves forward. Lead routing in turn, by territory, or to whoever is on duty.

items.title: CRM data migration
items.body: Your records are moved from your current system or from spreadsheets, and duplicates are merged. The old system stays read-only during the switch.

items.title: CRM integration
items.body: The phone system is connected to the CRM, so calls are logged on the record with the recording. Email sequences run with rules that stop them.

items.title: Automation and AI agents
items.body: Documented automations between tools, and AI agents on Claude or OpenAI that write call notes, qualify inbound leads and draft follow-ups for a rep to approve.

items.title: Training on your own data
items.body: Training sessions use your own data and are recorded for the team. Handover notes say how each piece runs and who to call about it.

items.title: A revenue scoreboard
items.body: Targets per rep and per team, a live leaderboard, and the reports the owner reads, pulled from the CRM and the phone system.

blocks.h2: The CRM implementation process, step by step.
blocks.intro: At Stacktik, the written proposal is your CRM implementation plan.

items.title: A free first call
items.body: We go through what you use today, what isn't working, and whether the next step is software, implementation, both, or nothing yet. There is no obligation.

items.title: A shortlist and a written proposal
items.body: We map how leads, calls and follow-ups move through your team, then shortlist two or three CRMs with the monthly cost of each.

items.title: CRM setup in your account
items.body: The subscription is in your name, bought through our partner programs or direct. We build the pipeline stages and lead routing through an admin seat you create.

items.title: Your data moved over
items.body: Records come across from your current system or spreadsheets, and duplicates are merged. The old system is read-only during the switch, then yours to close.

items.title: Calling, outreach and reporting connected
items.body: The phone system and outreach tool are connected to the CRM, and reports pull from all three, so the numbers update without anyone typing.

items.title: Training and handover
items.body: Your team is trained on the setup and given written handover notes. Then you revoke our admin seat.

blocks.intro: There are two separate numbers, both on the Stacktik proposal: what the software costs you each month, and what our work costs.

items.title: Plan and seat count
items.body: The software is on the vendor's own plan and pricing. The monthly figure depends on the plan and the number of seats.

items.title: How much data moves
items.body: Moving records out of one current system is a different job from pulling them out of several spreadsheets.

items.title: How many tools connect
items.body: A CRM on its own is a smaller project than a CRM with a phone system, an outreach tool and a reporting dashboard connected to it.

items.title: Automation, AI agents and custom tools
items.body: Automations between tools, AI agents for routine steps, and any internal tool or connector we build are scoped and quoted on the same proposal.

items.title: Additions and ongoing support
items.body: The proposal says what is in scope, what is not, and what an addition would cost. Support after handover is optional and monthly, with its own fee.

blocks.h2: How to choose a CRM implementation consultant or partner.
blocks.intro: CRM consulting ranges from one vendor's own onboarding to a full build across several tools.

items.title: Scope and fee in writing
items.body: Ask for the scope, what is out of scope, the fee and what counts as done before work starts.

items.title: One named person on the work
items.body: Ask who builds it. At Stacktik one technical RevOps consultant is the same person on the call, the proposal and the build.

items.title: Vendor relationships disclosed
items.body: Ask whether the vendor pays the consultant. Our proposal states our relationship with each vendor next to its price.

items.title: Software and setup kept separate
items.body: A consultant should not tie the two together. Buy direct and hire us only for the implementation, or buy through us and set up yourself.

items.title: Work across every tool
items.body: The CRM is the system your other tools connect to. Check that the consultant sets up calling, outreach and reporting across every tool, not one vendor's.

items.title: Limits stated up front
items.body: Ask what the consultant does not do. We do not usually take on Salesforce or ERP migrations, write your email copy, or run your outbound.

platforms.h2: CRM software: the platforms we set up.
platforms.intro: For teams choosing a CRM in Canada or the United States, these are the ones Stacktik works with.

faq.a: The cost of a CRM implementation has two parts: the software, on the vendor's own plan and pricing, and the implementation work. Stacktik quotes the work as a fixed fee, in writing, before it starts, with what is in scope, what is not and what an addition would cost.

faq.q: What are the steps in a CRM implementation plan?
faq.a: At Stacktik, the steps in implementing a CRM are a first call, a shortlist and written proposal, then the work the proposal scopes: setup in your account, data migration, connecting calling, outreach and reporting, training and handover.

faq.q: How do I choose a CRM implementation consultant?
faq.a: Choose a CRM consultant who puts the scope, the fee and what counts as done in writing before work starts. Then check who does the build, whether a vendor pays them, whether they connect the tools around the CRM, and whether you can buy the software and the setup separately.

faq.q: What is the best CRM for a small business in Canada?
faq.a: There is no single best CRM for every small business in Canada. The right one fits how your team sells, at a monthly cost you see before you commit.

faq.q: How does CRM data migration work when we switch CRMs?
faq.a: In a CRM migration, your records are moved from the current system or from spreadsheets into the new CRM, and duplicates are merged. With Stacktik, the old system stays read-only during the switch and is then yours to close. Salesforce and ERP migrations are not usually in scope.

faq.q: Can Stacktik be our CRM implementation partner if we already bought the CRM?
faq.a: Yes. Stacktik works as your CRM implementation partner whether you bought the CRM direct, bought it through Stacktik, or have not chosen one yet. You can buy direct and hire us only for the implementation, or buy through us and run the setup yourself.
